subject: Nebula Health - hosted API: ephemeral cache, backups, and erasure workflow
messages:

Subject: Hosted API: questions on ephemeral cache + backups for EU data

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Our security team had a few follow-ups specifically around ephemeral inference caches and backup snapshots for the hosted API in the EU region. They asked for clarification on: 

- How long does Redwood retain in-memory / KV cache contents and intermediate request context for hosted API calls?
- What happens to cached content and logs when a tenant requests a full data erasure? Are backups and snapshots purged as well?
- Is there an SLA or timeline we can include in our vendor risk assessment for complete removal?

Can you confirm and, if possible, include a short timeline we can share with our legal/compliance folks? If helpful, we can coordinate a call.

Appreciate it — Emma

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Wright <emma.wright@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-17T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on ephemeral cache + backups for EU data

Hi Emma — thanks for the follow-up. Looping in Monica (CS) and Hannah (Security) for any additional compliance details. Below is a compact summary you can paste into your vendor RRA; I also attached a one-page retention matrix and our SOC2 summary for reference.

High-level answers (hosted API, EU region):

1) Ephemeral/kV cache and inference context
- Purpose: We keep per-request prefixes/KV cache only to service low-latency continued conversations and to accelerate repeated requests where permitted by contract.
- Default TTL: 60 minutes of inactivity (sliding), configurable down to 0 minutes (ephemeral) at account level for customers under a managed contract.
- Visibility: Cached content is stored encrypted in transient memory and ephemeral SSD-backed caches; it is not written to long-term object storage unless explicitly configured (e.g., for conversation history).

2) Backups and snapshots
- Regular backups: snapshots for disaster recovery are taken in the region and retained on an immutable cycle by default (90 days).
- Inclusion: Snapshots do not contain separate copies of in-memory KV caches unless a customer has enabled persistent conversation logging. Snapshots capture persisted tables, blob storage, and system metadata.

3) Deletion / full erasure workflow (tenant-initiated)
- Request intake: Erasure requests are submitted via Support (see link below) or through the Console erase workflow.
- Purge: We initiate an asynchronous purge across hot and cold storage within 24 hours. For persisted blobs and DB entries we mark records as tombstoned immediately and schedule physical overwrite/compaction.
- Backup/Snapshot treatment: Active snapshots containing customer data are flagged for expedited deletion; snapshots that are part of immutable backup windows are eligible for deletion after a snapshot validation (typically within the same 90-day cycle).
- Confirmation: We provide an erasure certificate when the purge completes.

4) SLA / timeline (typical)
- Hot layers / DB entries: tombstone within 24 hours, irreversible overwrite during the next compaction window (within 7–30 days depending on storage tier).
- Backups & snapshots: targeted purge within 30–90 days depending on snapshot age and retention policy; expedited deletion available under enterprise contract where snapshots can be zeroed within 30 days.

Notes & exceptions:
- Minimal metadata (transactional billing records, invoice references) is retained for up to 12 months to satisfy billing and regulatory obligations in certain jurisdictions; that metadata is confined to an audit-only store and can be redacted on a case-by-case basis with legal review.
- For EU-hosted accounts we pin data to EU regions by default and use region-scoped encryption keys.

Attachments: data-retention-matrix-20280417.csv, redwood-soc2-summary-2028.pdf

Links: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/NB-4721 (erasure intake)

If you want I can convert the timeline into a short SLA paragraph for your vendor pack. Happy to hop on a quick call if Hannah/Monica should join.

Thanks Vivek — that is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions from our security engineering lead: 

- When you say 'tombstone' and 'compaction', can you confirm whether there is any point at which deleted data could be reconstructed from older snapshots or journaling before compaction completes?
- For the EU region specifically, are backups and snapshots encrypted with region-scoped KMS keys (managed by us or by Redwood)?
- Is there a separate retention policy for access logs and audit logs? Those are often requested by our privacy team in erasure exhibits.

If you can add the exact phrasing we can include it in Appendix A of our assessment. Also — can we get an ETA on the erasure certificate delivery timeframe for a standard deletion request?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Emma

Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on ephemeral cache + backups for EU data

Emma — good questions. Answers below with suggested vendor-assessment wording. Hannah added a short technical note after the bulleted list.

1) Reconstruction risk from pre-compaction artifacts
Suggested phrasing: "Redwood places records into a tombstoned state immediately upon erasure request. Tombstoning prevents application-layer reads. Under normal operating processes, background compaction and zeroing remove tombstoned data from physical storage within 7–30 days depending on storage tier; as such, the window in which raw bits might be reconstructable is limited to that period. Redwood offers an expedited compaction option under enterprise contracts to reduce that window to 30 days or less."

2) Encryption & KMS for EU backups
Suggested phrasing: "All backups and snapshots for EU-hosted tenants are encrypted at-rest using AES-256. Customer keys can be managed via the customer's KMS (BYOK) or via Redwood-managed regional KMS; key scope and rotation policies are configurable during procurement and are noted in the security appendix."

3) Access logs & audit logs retention
Suggested phrasing: "Access and audit logs are retained for 90 days by default. Logs used for billing/audit may be retained up to 12 months in an immutable audit store. On erasure, logs containing direct customer content are redacted where possible; metadata necessary for legal or billing obligations is retained only as legally required and minimized where feasible."

4) Erasure certificate ETA
Suggested phrasing: "For standard deletion requests on the hosted API, Redwood issues a preliminary acknowledgement within 24 hours and delivers a completion certificate within 30–90 days depending on the snapshot retention state. Expedited processing is available as a contracted feature with a target completion of 30 days."

Technical note (Hannah): "To expand on compaction: we run region-local block-level GC cycles. Tombstoning removes logical pointers immediately; physical blocks are zeroed or re-encrypted during GC. For customers who require proof of zeroing, we can provide a binding attestation under NDA that details the compaction window for the specific account."

Next steps: Monica will open a support ticket to record this request and can add expedited deletion as a line item if you'd like.
